title: Fed’s preferred inflation gauge shows core prices rose 3.3% annually in July
summary: In July, the personal consumption expenditures price index, which is the Federal Reserve's preferred measure of inflation, indicated a 3.3% annual increase in core prices. This figure was slightly below the anticipated rise of 3.6% over a 12-month period, as projected by economists from Dow Jones. Additionally, a monthly increase of 0.1% was expected, reflecting ongoing concerns about inflation trends in the economy.
shadowing: The personal consumption expenditures price index is crucial for understanding inflation.
Economists surveyed by Dow Jones provided their expectations for price increases.
A rise of 3.3% annually indicates persistent inflationary pressures.
Monthly increases in core prices can impact monetary policy decisions.
The Federal Reserve closely monitors these inflation metrics.
